launch_bound.note: heuristic: busy fraction = union of kernel intervals / measured wall of the active updates (profiler overhead inflates wall)

padding.note: prompt = the columns of prompt_ids that split_batch hands every micro-batch: today the full batch width W (this is what the reader / Gemma-front adapter / b3g2 thinker see). For the plain arms the transformer itself already trims to the micro-batch's widest row (plain_tf_steps.py loss: W = max(2 + len + target)), so for "seq" (= prompt + 2 + target) today is "own widest". Cost ratios are rows x width (linear) and rows x width^2 (attention-like) of today over sorted + own widest, not seconds.
